cim_eredeti: Portland Public Schools discusses generative AI use in classrooms
szoveg_eredeti:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KATU) — The Portland Public Schools policy committee on Monday night received an inventory of the generative artificial intelligence systems used in the district, and heard some recommendations for forming a policy around AI.

The update came after the school board voted earlier this year to pause the use and expansion of generative AI technologies across the district.

That resolution paused new contracts, software licenses, pilot programs and procurement actions primarily related to generative AI.

READ MORE | Portland school board vote on pausing AI expansion plan

It also stopped the expansion of existing AI programs while district leaders conduct a comprehensive review of current technology use.

The recommendations that policy committee members heard on Monday included teaching students how to use the technology to enhance how they learn, rather than let it do the work for them, as well as lessons on data privacy.

Committee members also heard a recommendation about creating a policy that can adapt as AI technology advances.

They also discussed teaching students how to recognize AI-generated content and how to interact with it.

Dr. Kristin Moon, the Director of Educator Professional Learning with the district, said they've been looking to other districts across the country on when to start teaching students AI literacy and how to be "critical consumers." She said that starts for some districts as young as 6th through 8th grade.

"Knowing how to have healthy technology habits, even knowing ‘hey, this chatbot is designed to give you back affirmative things' ... [or] might be encouraging you to do things that are actually really unhealthy and not good for you as humans," said Moon.

KATU reached out to the district to ask what happens next, and when new guidelines could be in place. We are waiting to hear back from officials.
